THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Marathon County set new zoning rules for battery storage and data centers and punted a contentious wind energy resolution back to committee, while Wausau advanced a tax increment bond for a downtown development and launched a police deputy-chief search tied to future leadership succession.

  • Marathon County adopted a 500-foot setback rule for battery energy storage systems and a temporary moratorium on data centers, then referred the Hub City Wind resolution back to the Executive Committee for a clearer recommendation at September's meeting.
  • The Wausau Finance Committee approved a tax increment revenue bond for the Foundry on Third development and a 2026 budget workshop calendar with four sessions beginning October 5.
  • The Wausau Police & Fire Commission approved a deputy-chief promotional process launching this fall — applications open in September, with a decision expected at the December commission meeting — as part of police chief succession planning.
  • Weston's Board of Trustees approved a $1.29 million waterworks revenue bond and voted to hold trustee pay flat for the 2027–2029 term at $7,200 for trustees and $8,400 for the village president.
  • Weston's Parks Committee heard a concept for a 30,000-square-foot indoor community space at Kennedy Park from Everest Youth Hockey, agreeing to further study with no village funding committed.
  • Kronenwetter's Village Board is set to vote on accepting the Village Clerk's resignation at a special meeting called August 27.

Coming up: Wausau's Committee of the Whole meets Wednesday, September 2 at 5:30 p.m. — likely the week's highest-stakes session — while the Economic Development Committee convenes Tuesday, September 1 at 5:30 p.m., worth watching given ongoing downtown financing discussions.
